params.question: In the pathogenesis of tuberculosis, what prevents progression from latent infection to active disease in 90–95 percent of immunocompetent individuals?

answers.text: Direct killing of bacilli by alveolar surfactant proteins

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alveolar surfactant does not kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The bacilli survive within macrophages by blocking lysosome fusion — containment requires the adaptive immune response.

answers.text: Antibody-mediated opsonisation by B lymphocytes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Humoral immunity plays a minor role in TB defence. Cell-mediated immunity — specifically the CD4-positive Th1 response releasing interferon-gamma — is the primary containment mechanism.

answers.text: Granuloma formation driven by a CD4-positive Th1 immune response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. CD4-positive T cells release interferon-gamma, activating macrophages and forming structured granulomas that wall off the bacilli and maintain latency.

answers.text: Mycolic acid degradation by neutrophil-derived enzymes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mycolic acids in the TB cell wall resist degradation — that resistance is what makes the organism acid-fast. It is the adaptive immune response, not neutrophil enzymes, that contains the infection.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four stages: macrophage engulfment → Th1 activation → granuloma formation → latency. The granuloma, maintained by interferon-gamma, is what keeps 90–95% of infections dormant.
Well done. The Th1-driven granuloma is the cornerstone of TB containment — when this immune response weakens, latent TB reactivates.

interactions.label: Under NTEP screening, all four symptoms — cough, fever, night sweats, and weight

params.question: Under NTEP screening, all four symptoms — cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss — must be present simultaneously before initiating a tuberculosis evaluation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: That is incorrect. The NTEP guideline states that any single symptom — cough, fever, night sweats, or weight loss — persisting for two weeks or more is sufficient to initiate tuberculosis evaluation. All four need not be present.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The NTEP four-symptom screen requires only one of these symptoms lasting two weeks or more to trigger systematic evaluation. Requiring all four simultaneously would dangerously delay diagnosis in India's high-burden setting.

interactions.label: A 48-year-old man in India presents with cough for four weeks, low-grade fever,

params.question: A 48-year-old man in India presents with cough for four weeks, low-grade fever, weight loss, and haemoptysis. Which differential diagnosis approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: Prioritise community-acquired pneumonia because haemoptysis suggests an acute bacterial aetiology

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Community-acquired pneumonia typically presents acutely, not over four weeks. In India, chronic cough with constitutional symptoms places tuberculosis highest in the differential.

answers.text: Place pulmonary tuberculosis at the top of the differential and simultaneously investigate for lung malignancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In India's high-prevalence setting, TB leads the hierarchy for chronic cough with constitutional symptoms. Haemoptysis in a patient over 40 also warrants a chest X-ray to exclude coexisting malignancy.

answers.text: Order sputum culture for tuberculosis only and defer further workup until results return in six to eight weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Waiting six to eight weeks for culture alone delays diagnosis. The differential should include malignancy alongside TB, and rapid molecular testing (CBNAAT) is now the first-line investigation.

answers.text: Treat empirically for fungal pneumonia because haemoptysis points to aspergilloma

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aspergilloma is far less common than tuberculosis in India. The differential ranks TB first; fungal infections sit lower unless immunosuppression or a pre-existing cavity is documented.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: in India, for any adult with chronic cough, fever, and weight loss, pulmonary TB sits at the top of the differential. Haemoptysis over age 40 mandates a chest X-ray because malignancy and TB can coexist.
Exactly. A differential diagnosis is a ranked probability distribution — in India, TB leads, but haemoptysis in older patients demands parallel investigation for malignancy.

interactions.label: An HIV-positive patient with suspected tuberculosis shows 7 mm of induration on

params.question: An HIV-positive patient with suspected tuberculosis shows 7 mm of induration on the Mantoux test at 72 hours. How should this result be interpreted?

answers.text: Negative — the induration is below the standard 10 mm threshold for India

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 10 mm threshold applies to high-risk groups without immunosuppression. For HIV-positive patients, the threshold is lowered to 5 mm because their impaired immunity produces a weaker delayed-type hypersensitivity response.

answers.text: Positive — the threshold for HIV-positive patients is 5 mm of induration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In immunosuppressed patients including those with HIV, 5 mm or more of induration is considered positive. The lower threshold accounts for the reduced capacity to mount a tuberculin reaction.

answers.text: Inconclusive — the test must be repeated after at least three months of antiretroviral therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The result is interpretable now. At 7 mm in an HIV-positive patient, the test exceeds the 5 mm threshold and is positive. Delaying interpretation would delay diagnosis.

answers.text: False positive — likely caused by prior BCG vaccination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While BCG can cause false-positive Mantoux results, that does not override interpretation in an HIV-positive patient with clinical suspicion for TB. At 7 mm with a 5 mm threshold, this is a positive result.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Mantoux thresholds are risk-stratified: 5 mm for HIV-positive or immunosuppressed patients, 10 mm for high-risk groups in India including healthcare workers and contacts, and 15 mm for low-risk individuals.
Well done. The three-tiered threshold — 5, 10, and 15 mm — must be applied to the patient's risk category. In HIV, the bar is lowest because anergy can suppress even a genuine reaction.

interactions.label: A 30-year-old woman on oral contraceptive pills is started on anti-tuberculosis

params.question: A 30-year-old woman on oral contraceptive pills is started on anti-tuberculosis therapy. Which drug interaction requires immediate counselling?

answers.text: Isoniazid inhibits cytochrome P450, raising oral contraceptive levels to toxic concentrations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Isoniazid is a weak CYP450 inhibitor, not a clinically significant one for oral contraceptives. It is rifampicin that powerfully induces CYP450, reducing contraceptive efficacy.

answers.text: Pyrazinamide competes with oestrogen for hepatic conjugation, causing breakthrough bleeding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pyrazinamide's principal risk is hepatotoxicity within the acidic macrophage environment. It does not significantly interact with oral contraceptives. Rifampicin is the drug that lowers contraceptive levels.

answers.text: Rifampicin induces cytochrome P450 enzymes, reducing oral contraceptive efficacy and risking unintended pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rifampicin is one of the most potent CYP450 inducers in clinical use. It accelerates metabolism of oral contraceptives, warfarin, and antiretrovirals. An alternative contraceptive method must be advised.

answers.text: Ethambutol blocks renal excretion of oestrogen metabolites, increasing thromboembolic risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ethambutol's critical adverse effect is optic neuritis from inhibition of arabinosyl transferase. It has no significant interaction with oestrogen metabolism. The correct concern is rifampicin's CYP450 induction.

overallFeedback.feedback: Rifampicin powerfully induces cytochrome P450 enzymes, lowering plasma levels of oral contraceptives, warfarin, and antiretroviral drugs. Screen all co-medications before prescribing and counsel patients accordingly.
Exactly. Rifampicin's CYP450 induction is one of the most important drug interactions in TB therapy — always screen co-medications before starting treatment.

interactions.label: A tuberculosis patient is found to have resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and

params.question: A tuberculosis patient is found to have resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and levofloxacin, but remains sensitive to bedaquiline and linezolid. How is this resistance pattern classified?

answers.text: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: MDR-TB is defined as resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin. This patient's resistance extends beyond that to include a fluoroquinolone, placing the classification one step further along the spectrum.

answers.text: Pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Pre-XDR TB is MDR-TB with additional resistance to any fluoroquinolone. Since bedaquiline and linezolid remain effective, it has not reached XDR status.

answers.text: Extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: XDR-TB requires MDR plus fluoroquinolone resistance plus resistance to bedaquiline or linezolid. This patient retains sensitivity to both, so the classification is pre-XDR, not XDR.

answers.text: Isoniazid mono-resistant tuberculosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mono-resistance refers to resistance to a single first-line drug. This patient has resistance to three agents — isoniazid, rifampicin, and levofloxacin — which far exceeds mono-resistance.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the spectrum: MDR = resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin. Pre-XDR = MDR plus fluoroquinolone resistance. XDR = pre-XDR plus resistance to bedaquiline or linezolid. Classify by what the organism resists.
Well done. The resistance spectrum runs MDR → pre-XDR → XDR. Each step adds resistance to a critical drug class, narrowing treatment options and requiring NTEP specialist referral.
